meta.label: exploratory (post-hoc; not in the locked design §9)
meta.interval: Welch-type 95% interval on the log scale: the CPU times come from the side-study sessions and the GPU times from the main rounds, different sessions in different rounds, so the two sets of per-round values are unpaired (Welch-Satterthwaite df); no interval with fewer than two rounds on either side
meta.definition: Post-hoc analyses for the baseline-confound paper; none is part of the locked design (section 9). protocol_check: side-study Polars 1.44.2 time / main-round polars time on the same host. decomp: for c1 and c2, the speedup of a host divided by the speedup of the reference host, split into the CPU engine's and the GPU engine's host / reference time ratios over one matched query set. sensitivity: C1 (locked design, t-interval over rounds) next to E1 (Polars 2.0.0 CPU / Polars GPU, Welch-type). Every interval except C1's is Welch-type on the log scale (unpaired rounds).

meta.label: exploratory (post-hoc; not in the locked design §9), sensitivity
meta.definition: E1 / K1 and E4 / K4 per host, suite and scale: the exploratory Polars 2.0.0 CPU / GPU ratio divided by the protocol check (side-study Polars 1.44.2 / main-round polars), computed over the same queries. Equals B_matched x C: B = Polars 2.0.0 / 1.44.2 in the side-study rounds, C = main-round Polars CPU 1.44.2 / GPU (C1, or C4 for E4), each paired within its rounds. Interval: se^2 = s_B^2/n_B + s_C^2/n_C with Welch-Satterthwaite df. The point estimate is asserted equal to E1 / K1 (identity_gap, 1e-9). verdict_*: gpu_faster / cpu_faster / inconclusive from the interval against 1.
